1	# s27 assessment: fixture analysis for the agreement margins (2026-11-04)
2	
3	**Scope.** This was an offline step. I used no network, contacted no box, ran no git commands and read no credentials. The Bash tool was denied in this session, so I wrote every file with the file tool and hashed nothing. I wrote only into `science/s27/`.
4	
5	**What I read.**
6	- s13 (`FINAL.json`, assessment), s15 (`SHAPES.json`, assessment), s26 (assessment, prompt) and s07 §A–§D; for s16–s25 I worked from their assessments' K1–K3 passages.
7	- The run6 calibration brief (`science/s06/CALIBRATION_BRIEF.md`), the physical card's plan (`20261103-0124-tree/out/work/seed-20261103/R1/physical/1fffee1a/producer.md`, called PC below) and `dut/pipeline/m5/SCHEMAS.md:115–203`, whole.
8	- The scorer's error code `dut/pipeline/m5/score_comparison.py:469–504`.
9	- The blind-01 run11 unit manifest and intake inventory (`experiments/blind-01/m5/run11/agent/harness/units.json`, `.../intake/data.json`).
10	
11	**Verdict.** A fixture run is justified and fits the limits.
12	- I sealed a tolerance rule for every margin the main comparison needs (`TOLERANCE_RULE.md`, `tolerance_rule.json`).
13	- The fixture run (`fixture_design.json`, `FIXTURE_BRIEF.md`) only records values. All 12 of its comparisons are `exact`.
14	- The error budget is **partly** feasible. Analysis bounds serialization, determinism and the FFT roundoff (loosely). Two sources can only be measured, not bounded: GPU nondeterminism and the effect of `-use_fast_math` on voxel assignment.
15	- Next: **m5**, projected about USD 7, worst case USD 14.5, 1–3 h expected.
16	
17	## A. The main inputs, and the fixtures
18	
19	**Main comparison (s13, s15).**
20	- **Arms** (`s13/FINAL.json:2–4`; `s13/ASSESSMENT.md:13–17`):
21	  - A0: CPU MEGADOCK at 3600 rotations;
22	  - A1: GPU MEGADOCK, identical settings;
23	  - A2: GPU at 54000 rotations (`-D`).
24	- **Margin comparisons:**
25	  - K1, K2 and K3 are A1 against A0 (`FINAL.json:7–9`). Each is `per_input_all`, `paired_replicate`, `all_pairs` (`s15/SHAPES.json:2–4`).
26	  - K6 and K7 carry `0.01 + 2·eps_eval` (`s13/ASSESSMENT.md:51–57`).
27	- **Inputs** (`s13/ASSESSMENT.md:66`; `m5/BRIEF.md:3`): the four seed cases, each the apo pairing of PINDER `2024-02` (`m5/b01_materials/BRIEF_run1.md:56–158`):
28	  - `1aua__A1_P24280--1aua__A2_P24280:apo`
29	  - `1ax2__A1_P16404--1ax2__A2_P16404:apo`
30	  - `1dv1__A1_P24182--1dv1__B1_P24182:apo`
31	  - `1nr5__A1_P07547--1nr5__A2_P07547:apo`
32	- **Prepared hashes and settings.** The prepared hashes are at `s06/CALIBRATION_BRIEF.md:340–343`. The shared settings are `-N 50 -t 1 -v 1.2 -e 1.0 -d 1.0 -a -45.0 -b 1.0 -f 3` (`:387–391`).
33	
34	**Fixtures chosen.** These are the holo test-set monomer pairs of four PINDER `2024-02` systems. They are the non-seed systems of the same blind-01 unit manifest that held the seed cases: run11 `units.json` lists 16 units, with ids at lines 4–844, and the seed cases sit at its indices 3, 5, 9 and 15 (`BRIEF_run1.md:48`). URLs, bytes and SHA-256 come from blind-01 run11 `intake/data.json`.
35	
36	| input id | PINDER system | receptor / ligand source (bytes) | native (bytes) | data.json lines |
37	|---|---|---|---|---|
38	| f1a19 | `1a19__A1_P11540--1a19__B1_P11540` | 58320 / 58320 | 116559 | 14662–14667, 28000–28014 |
39	| f1dtd | `1dtd__A1_P48052--1dtd__B1_P81511` | 192132 / 38313 | 230364 | 15184–15189, 28090–28104 |
40	| f1glj | `1glj__A1_P0A6F3--1glj__B1_P0A6F3` | 316791 / 316791 | 633501 | 15598–15603, 28180–28194 |
41	| f1ht8 | `1ht8__A1_P05979--1ht8__B1_P05979` | 362718 / 362718 | 725355 | 15760–15765, 28252–28266 |
42	
43	**Same numerical path.** Each fixture runs exactly the main arms' code path:
44	- **Binaries and flags.** The same two MEGADOCK binaries are built from the same commit with the same flags (single-precision FFTW `-lfftw3f` on the CPU; cuFFT with `-use_fast_math` on the GPU; `s06/CALIBRATION_BRIEF.md:361–369`). The same command lines and environment are used (`OMP_NUM_THREADS=26`, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`; `:387–391`), as are the same 3600-rotation set, voxel size and scoring settings.
45	- **FFT path.** It is the same FFT correlation, translational reductions and ranking to 50 rows.
46	- **Reconstruction and evaluation.** The same `decoygen` and model assembly are used (`:393`), and the same PINDER BiotiteDockQ evaluator (`:330`) with R/L mapping.
47	- **Inputs.** The preparation rule is the same (chain field to R/L; `:336`), and the inputs are the same kind of file: PINDER monomer PDBs.
48	- **Size range.** Monomer sizes span 38–363 KB, against 150–277 KB for the main prepared sources (`BRIEF_run1.md:75, 102, 129–130, 156`). The grid sizes therefore bracket the main cases.
49	- **Chain mapping.** Three fixtures are homodimers, like all four seed cases. f1dtd adds a heterodimer.
50	
51	**The one difference: holo, not apo.** These are bound conformations. In holo inputs the identity rotation is near-native, so the fixtures' DockQ values will sit higher than the seed cases'. This changes which poses are evaluated, not the arithmetic. I chose holo because blind-01's records pin these files by hash, while the apo files of the four disjoint systems cannot be identified from the records without the index.
52	
53	**Disjointness rule.** A fixture is admissible iff all three hold:
54	1. its PINDER system id differs from each seed id;
55	2. none of its UniProt accessions is among the seed accessions {P24280, P16404, P24182, P07547};
56	3. none of its source, prepared or native files has the SHA-256 of any file recorded for a seed case. That covers the sources, prepared files, natives, holo test-set members and alternates in `BRIEF_run1.md:72–273`, and `s06:340–343`.
57	
58	Rule (2) excludes every structure of a seed protein, including the seed systems' own holo and AlphaFold files. The fixtures' accessions are P11540, P48052, P81511, P0A6F3 and P05979, so (1) and (2) hold. I checked (3) by comparing the listed hashes by eye; no Bash was available. The prepared fixture hashes do not exist yet, and the run's setup records them.
59	
60	The fixture run also never fetches or reads any seed file. Its brief tells setup not to (`FIXTURE_BRIEF.md`, comparison request).
61	
62	## B. Analytic error budget
63	
64	Notation: u = 2^-24 ≈ 5.96e-8 (binary32).
65	
66	**Outputs the margins concern:**
67	- `transforms`: main K1 identity;
68	- `coords`: main K1 eps_xyz;
69	- `scores`: main K2;
70	- `dockq`: main K3, and through eps_eval, K6/K7.
71	
72	| # | Source | Affects | Expected size for a correct arm | Evidence | Fixtures measure? |
73	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
74	| 1 | Floating-point precision. Both FFT paths are binary32. | scores | Worst case, per correlation peak: A_rel(N) = (3·log2 N³ + 1)·5u·N^1.5 relative, about 0.02–0.06 for N = 100–200. The typical normwise size is about (log2 n)·u ≈ 1e-6 to 1e-5. | `-lfftw3f` and `-lcufft` (`s06:363, 369`). The bound form follows the FFT normwise error result of Higham, *Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms*, 2nd ed., §24.1. **This is recalled, not a repository file, and was not re-read (no network).** The √n factor converts a normwise bound into a per-element bound and is my derivation. | Yes, as the combined score difference (F-K4, F-K6). Analysis gives only the loose ceiling the rule checks against. |
75	| 2 | Reduction and summation order (FFTW vs cuFFT plans; GPU translational max reductions). | scores; transforms at near-ties | Scores: the same order as #1. Transforms change only where two candidates' scores are within that error, at rank ties or cutoff membership. The size cannot be bounded without the score landscape. | No file states the plans. "Tie mismatch fails this strict gate" (PC:58). | Yes (F-K1, F-K3). |
76	| 3 | Nondeterministic GPU kernels. | all GPU outputs | Unknown in magnitude. Only file hashes exist. | GPU `docking.out`: 39 distinct SHA-256 in 40 files. CPU: one hash per case in 20/20 (`s07/ASSESSMENT.md:116–118`). | Yes, GPU self-agreement (F-K3, F-K6, F-K9, F-K12). |
77	| 4 | Compiler flags (`-use_fast_math` on the GPU build only). | scores; transforms | Approximate trig and flush-to-zero perturb rotated ligand coordinates by roughly 1e-6 relative (about 3e-5 Å at 30 Å). A grid assignment flips when an atom lies within that distance of a voxel boundary (`-v 1.2`): roughly 5e-5 per atom per rotation. This is my estimate, not a measurement. Each flip moves one atom's score contribution. That cannot be bounded without MEGADOCK's scoring source, which is not in the repository. | `s06:360, 366` ("retain published -O3 and -use_fast_math") | Only in cross-arm agreement (F-K4, F-K1). The effect is deterministic, so GPU self-agreement does not show it. |
78	| 5 | Library and driver versions. | all | Controlled, not measured. CUDA 12.8, driver 570.148.08, H100 PCIe (`s07:74–75`). FFTW is the distro package; its version is not in the files I read. | Rebuilding on this box type reproduced the CPU binary hash `4b85db6e…` in run4 and run6 (`s07:94`). The pipeline records executables and library hashes (`SCHEMAS.md:171`). | No. The rule (§3 step 4) requires identity between the fixture run and the main run. |
79	| 6 | Seeds. | none | 0. The FFT search is exhaustive and deterministic, with no random sampling. `order_seed` only orders invocations (`SCHEMAS.md:172`). | "deterministic repeats do not increase biological sample size" (PC:30). CPU byte-reproducible (`s07:116`). | Confirmed by CPU self-agreement (F-K2, F-K5). |
80	| 7 | CPU threading (26 OpenMP threads). | CPU outputs | 0 observed. | CPU 20/20 identical in run6 under the same environment (`s07:116`; `s06:387`). | Yes (F-K2, F-K5, F-K8). |
81	| 8 | Text serialization. | scores; coords | Scores: one unit of the last printed digit (atol = 10^-d, d read from the files by the rule). Coordinates: PDB `%8.3f` gives 0.001 Å. `decoygen` is one CPU binary for every arm (`fixture_design.json` commands), so identical transform rows give identical coordinates. | `s06:393`; run6 validation reads 7-field rows (`m5/run6/agent/harness/run_command.sh:125–141`) | Coordinates: yes (F-K7–F-K9, on pairs with identical transforms). Score print resolution: read from the files. |
82	| 9 | Evaluator. | dockq | 0 for byte-identical models (deterministic CPU code). If coordinates differ by at most 0.002 Å, the continuous DockQ terms move by at most about 0.0005. Each flipped native contact moves Fnat by 1/N_c, which is 1/(3·N_c) in DockQ. This uses DockQ = (Fnat + 1/(1+(iRMS/1.5)²) + 1/(1+(LRMS/8.5)²))/3 (Basu & Wallner 2016, **recalled, not a repository file**). The absolute accuracy against an independent implementation (PC:59) is not measurable on this route and stays an uncertainty. | Run4 evaluator: 16 walls, max 2.573 s (`s26/ASSESSMENT.md:38`) | Repeatability: yes (F-K11 on identical CPU models; F-K10 and F-K12 on pairs with identical transforms). Accuracy: no. |
83	| 10 | Shared hardware state between parts | all | None expected for deterministic code. | Declared residual (`SCHEMAS.md:116`) | Covered by the self-agreement pairs. |
84	
85	**Summary.**
86	- **Measured by the fixtures:** #2, #3, #4 and #7, together with the realised size of #1.
87	- **Bounded only by analysis:** #1 (as the loose ceiling A_rel), #6 and #8 (resolution units).
88	- **Controlled by identity checks:** #5.
89	- **Unbounded and kept as uncertainty:** #9's absolute accuracy.
90	
91	So the budget is `partly` feasible on `fixtures_and_analysis`.
92	
93	**What the fixtures cannot do.** They cannot make the card's exact transform-identity criterion achievable. If GPU self-agreement fails on the transforms, a correct GPU arm will fail the exact gate with no CPU involvement. The rule reports that as flag G_T and does not relax the criterion (PC:66).
94	
95	## C. Tolerance rule (sealed now)
96	
97	The full rule is in `TOLERANCE_RULE.md`. `tolerance_rule.json` has one item per margin: M1 to M6.
98	- **M1, K1 transform identity:** stays `exact` (no margin). The fixtures only set the flags X_T, C_T and G_T.
99	- **M2, K1 coordinates:**
100	  - `eps_xyz = up2(max(0.001 Å, 2·Mxyz))`, where Mxyz is the maximum coordinate error over pairs whose transforms are byte-identical.
101	  - Defensible iff Mxyz ≤ 0.001 Å and every fixture has at least 4 CPU-self pairs.
102	- **M3, K2 scores:**
103	  - `atol = 10^-d` (the printed resolution) and `rtol = up2(max(2·MR, 1e-6))`. MR is the maximum relative score error over the cross, CPU-self and GPU-self pairs.
104	  - Defensible iff no count mismatch and, per fixture, every maximum ≤ A_rel(N_f).
105	- **M4, K3 DockQ:**
106	  - `eps_eval = up2(max(0.001, 2·Me))`, where Me is the maximum DockQ error over pairs with identical transforms.
107	  - Defensible iff eps_eval ≤ 0.01 and every fixture has at least 4 CPU-self pairs.
108	- **M5 and M6, K6/K7:** `0.01 + 2·eps_eval`. Defensible iff M4 is.
109	- **Run-level conditions:**
110	  - If the run fails (V0), every derived margin is indefensible.
111	  - If any fixture comparison has fewer than 4 present pairs on any fixture (Z), every derived margin is indefensible.
112	  - An indefensible margin keeps its uncertainty: the main run records that output with `exact` (errors recorded) and claims no tolerance.
113	- **Applying it without judgment:** a later step reads `C/comparison_scored.json` (agrees, missing, max_abs_error, max_rel_error per pair) and A0's fetched `docking.out` (d, N_f), evaluates the formulas, and copies the margins into the main design. After the main run it checks binary, library, driver and GPU identity against the fixture run's `comparison_compute.json` (§3).
114	
115	Every constant is in the rule's table. k = 2, 0.001 and 0.01 are DESIGN choices, each stated with its reason. Nothing in the rule reads a seed case's output.
116	
117	## D. The fixture run
118	
119	- **Design:** `fixture_design.json`, in the exact schema of `SCHEMAS.md:117–141`.
120	- **Arms:**
121	  - A0 is the published baseline: CPU standard plus reconstruction.
122	  - A1 is the GPU standard arm whose outputs K1–K3 compare.
123	  - A2 and A3 duplicate A0 and A1 with identical commands. This gives two self-agreement arms: CPU, and GPU, which matters because the GPU is the nondeterministic one.
124	  - The dense arm is not included. No fixture margin concerns it; eps_eval for K6/K7 is an evaluator property measured on A0–A3.
125	  - The commands are `megadock`/`megadock-gpu` with the run6 flags. Reconstruction is one `bash -c` loop over `decoygen` plus model assembly, because 50 `decoygen` calls exceed the 8-command limit.
126	- **Inputs:** the four fixtures only.
127	- **Outputs:** `transforms` and `scores` (regex selections of the 7-field rows of `docking.out`), `coords` (PDB columns 31–54 of `out/model_*.pdb`, natural order) and `dockq` (`eval/dockq.json`, a JSON array).
128	- **Metric:** the trusted wall, which is required (at least 1 metric) and is not compared.
129	- **Evaluator:** yes. K3, and through it K6/K7, need it. The native complexes are the evaluator's private data.
130	- **Comparisons:** 12, all `exact`: four outputs × {cross, CPU self, GPU self}.
131	  - They decide nothing used by the rule except byte identity, which is itself a recorded fact.
132	  - The scorer records max_abs_error and max_rel_error for `exact` comparisons too (`score_comparison.py:492–504`), so the rule gets its numbers from the trusted scorer and no agent computes one.
133	  - Exact checks have no margin, so they cannot bias the rule.
134	- **Schedule and limits:**
135	  - `replicates` 6 and `warmup` 1, so 7 rounds × 16 = 112 invocations.
136	  - `timeout_s` 1200 per arm part and evaluator `timeout_s` 900. Both are far above the expected walls and only cap a hang.
137	  - `budget_s` 12600, which is below 19800.
138	  - `order_seed` 27277, `bootstrap_seed` 27278 and `bootstrap_resamples` 1000 (unused, but required by the schema).
139	- **Projection.**
140	  - **Per invocation:** about 30 s of overhead (shakedown-m5 run20: job receipt median 8.0 s, comparison receipt median 29.5 s). On top of that come the arm walls:
141	    - CPU about 5–25 s, scaled by input size from run6's 9.0–14.5 s (`s07:38–41`);
142	    - GPU about 2–6 s;
143	    - the evaluator about 2–5 s (run4: 1.8–2.6 s).
144	  - **Evaluate stage:** about 112 × 30 s plus about 22 min of compute, roughly 78 min.
145	  - **Rest of the allocation:** intake, harness, the two builds plus the PINDER install, setup, anchors, the users step, fetches and scoring, about 35 min (run6's whole allocation was 2083 s, including about 10 min of jobs; `s07:214`).
146	  - **Expected:** about 1.9–2.2 h, or **USD 6.3–7.2** at USD 3.29/h.
147	  - **Worst case under the caps:** about 0.6 h + 3.5 h (`budget_s`) + 0.3 h ≈ 4.4 h, or **USD 14.5**. That is under USD 20 and inside the 6 h limit.
148	- **Main runs fit after:** USD 100 − 1.67 − 14.5 (worst) = USD 83.8 left. The physical card's whole plan is USD 49.48 (`s13/ASSESSMENT.md:86`), and an agreement run on four cases (about 1.5 h, about USD 5) fits before it. So the answer is yes.
149	- **Brief:** `FIXTURE_BRIEF.md`.
150	  - It holds the seed and materials addendum, written from the read text of `BRIEF_run1.md` with the file tool. No byte copy was possible, so the operator should confirm that its first 310 lines equal `BRIEF_run1.md` byte for byte.
151	  - It then has one section, `## Comparison request (science step s27)`.
152	  - That section and the view text state no margin, threshold, expected result or rule. I grepped both files for every sealed number of the design (900, 1200, 12600, 27277, 27278, 1000). The only hits outside the sealed fields are digit runs inside SHA-256 hex strings of the verbatim addendum.
153	
154	## E. What each fixture result decides
155	
156	- **All of M2–M4 defensible** (with M5 and M6):
157	  - The next step writes the main agreement design (s13 run 1: A0 and A1, the four seed cases, the same outputs) with K1 transforms `exact`, K1 coordinates `{abs: eps_xyz}`, K2 `{abs: atol, rel: rtol}` and K3 `{abs: eps_eval}`. It writes the main study design with K6/K7 `{abs: 0.01 + 2·eps_eval}`, gated by `given` on K1–K3.
158	  - The cost then follows s13 and the card.
159	- **G_T true (GPU transforms not self-reproducible on fixtures):**
160	  - The card's exact gate (PC:58) would very likely fail on the seed cases from GPU nondeterminism alone.
161	  - Relaxing it "requires new prospective plan" (PC:66). That is the owner's decision, so the next step stops with `needs_owner` before the main agreement run, rather than spending on a gate that the fixtures show a correct GPU arm cannot pass.
162	  - The margins M2–M4 still stand or fall by the rule.
163	- **Some of M2–M4 indefensible:** that comparison is recorded as `exact` with errors and reported as having no defensible tolerance, so agreement is unresolved for it.
164	  - Whether the acceleration and quality comparisons may still run ungated by it is the owner's decision. The card gates dense quality on agreement failure, and unresolved is not failure. So the next step returns `needs_owner` with the reasons the rule produced.
165	- **The fixture run fails (V0 or Z):**
166	  - On an infrastructure failure with no comparison data, one repeat of this exact design is justified within the remaining ceiling.
167	  - On a harness or evaluator defect, the next step reports it and identifies the contract or harness gap.
168	  - No margin is derived from a partial run.
169	
170	## F. Narrowing
171	
172	Unchanged: **no narrowing** (`NARROWING.md`). The fixtures are measuring instruments, not new cases. The seed's conclusions stay limited to its four cases.
173	
174	## Predictions and outcomes
175	
176	s26 sealed no predictions, so `outcomes.json` is `{"items": []}`. Sixteen predictions for the fixture run are sealed in `PREDICTIONS.md` and `predictions.json`.
177

# s27 assessment: fixture analysis for the agreement margins (2026-11-04)

**Scope.** This was an offline step. I used no network, contacted no box, ran no git commands and read no credentials. The Bash tool was denied in this session, so I wrote every file with the file tool and hashed nothing. I wrote only into `science/s27/`.

**What I read.**
- s13 (`FINAL.json`, assessment), s15 (`SHAPES.json`, assessment), s26 (assessment, prompt) and s07 §A–§D; for s16–s25 I worked from their assessments' K1–K3 passages.
- The run6 calibration brief (`science/s06/CALIBRATION_BRIEF.md`), the physical card's plan (`20261103-0124-tree/out/work/seed-20261103/R1/physical/1fffee1a/producer.md`, called PC below) and `dut/pipeline/m5/SCHEMAS.md:115–203`, whole.
- The scorer's error code `dut/pipeline/m5/score_comparison.py:469–504`.
- The blind-01 run11 unit manifest and intake inventory (`experiments/blind-01/m5/run11/agent/harness/units.json`, `.../intake/data.json`).

**Verdict.** A fixture run is justified and fits the limits.
- I sealed a tolerance rule for every margin the main comparison needs (`TOLERANCE_RULE.md`, `tolerance_rule.json`).
- The fixture run (`fixture_design.json`, `FIXTURE_BRIEF.md`) only records values. All 12 of its comparisons are `exact`.
- The error budget is **partly** feasible. Analysis bounds serialization, determinism and the FFT roundoff (loosely). Two sources can only be measured, not bounded: GPU nondeterminism and the effect of `-use_fast_math` on voxel assignment.
- Next: **m5**, projected about USD 7, worst case USD 14.5, 1–3 h expected.

## A. The main inputs, and the fixtures

**Main comparison (s13, s15).**

  - A1: GPU MEGADOCK, identical settings;
  - A2: GPU at 54000 rotations (`-D`).

- **Inputs** (`s13/ASSESSMENT.md:66`; `m5/BRIEF.md:3`): the four seed cases, each the apo pairing of PINDER `2024-02` (`m5/b01_materials/BRIEF_run1.md:56–158`):

  - `1dv1__A1_P24182--1dv1__B1_P24182:apo`

**Fixtures chosen.** These are the holo test-set monomer pairs of four PINDER `2024-02` systems. They are the non-seed systems of the same blind-01 unit manifest that held the seed cases: run11 `units.json` lists 16 units, with ids at lines 4–844, and the seed cases sit at its indices 3, 5, 9 and 15 (`BRIEF_run1.md:48`). URLs, bytes and SHA-256 come from blind-01 run11 `intake/data.json`.

**Same numerical path.** Each fixture runs exactly the main arms' code path:
- **Binaries and flags.** The same two MEGADOCK binaries are built from the same commit with the same flags (single-precision FFTW `-lfftw3f` on the CPU; cuFFT with `-use_fast_math` on the GPU; `s06/CALIBRATION_BRIEF.md:361–369`). The same command lines and environment are used (`OMP_NUM_THREADS=26`, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`; `:387–391`), as are the same 3600-rotation set, voxel size and scoring settings.
- **FFT path.** It is the same FFT correlation, translational reductions and ranking to 50 rows.
- **Reconstruction and evaluation.** The same `decoygen` and model assembly are used (`:393`), and the same PINDER BiotiteDockQ evaluator (`:330`) with R/L mapping.
- **Inputs.** The preparation rule is the same (chain field to R/L; `:336`), and the inputs are the same kind of file: PINDER monomer PDBs.
- **Size range.** Monomer sizes span 38–363 KB, against 150–277 KB for the main prepared sources (`BRIEF_run1.md:75, 102, 129–130, 156`). The grid sizes therefore bracket the main cases.
- **Chain mapping.** Three fixtures are homodimers, like all four seed cases. f1dtd adds a heterodimer.

**The one difference: holo, not apo.** These are bound conformations. In holo inputs the identity rotation is near-native, so the fixtures' DockQ values will sit higher than the seed cases'. This changes which poses are evaluated, not the arithmetic. I chose holo because blind-01's records pin these files by hash, while the apo files of the four disjoint systems cannot be identified from the records without the index.

**Disjointness rule.** A fixture is admissible iff all three hold:
1. its PINDER system id differs from each seed id;
2. none of its UniProt accessions is among the seed accessions {P24280, P16404, P24182, P07547};
3. none of its source, prepared or native files has the SHA-256 of any file recorded for a seed case. That covers the sources, prepared files, natives, holo test-set members and alternates in `BRIEF_run1.md:72–273`, and `s06:340–343`.

Rule (2) excludes every structure of a seed protein, including the seed systems' own holo and AlphaFold files. The fixtures' accessions are P11540, P48052, P81511, P0A6F3 and P05979, so (1) and (2) hold. I checked (3) by comparing the listed hashes by eye; no Bash was available. The prepared fixture hashes do not exist yet, and the run's setup records them.

The fixture run also never fetches or reads any seed file. Its brief tells setup not to (`FIXTURE_BRIEF.md`, comparison request).

- **Unbounded and kept as uncertainty:** #9's absolute accuracy.

So the budget is `partly` feasible on `fixtures_and_analysis`.

**What the fixtures cannot do.** They cannot make the card's exact transform-identity criterion achievable. If GPU self-agreement fails on the transforms, a correct GPU arm will fail the exact gate with no CPU involvement. The rule reports that as flag G_T and does not relax the criterion (PC:66).

## C. Tolerance rule (sealed now)

The full rule is in `TOLERANCE_RULE.md`. `tolerance_rule.json` has one item per margin: M1 to M6.
- **M1, K1 transform identity:** stays `exact` (no margin). The fixtures only set the flags X_T, C_T and G_T.
- **M2, K1 coordinates:**
  - `eps_xyz = up2(max(0.001 Å, 2·Mxyz))`, where Mxyz is the maximum coordinate error over pairs whose transforms are byte-identical.
  - Defensible iff Mxyz ≤ 0.001 Å and every fixture has at least 4 CPU-self pairs.
- **M3, K2 scores:**
  - `atol = 10^-d` (the printed resolution) and `rtol = up2(max(2·MR, 1e-6))`. MR is the maximum relative score error over the cross, CPU-self and GPU-self pairs.
  - Defensible iff no count mismatch and, per fixture, every maximum ≤ A_rel(N_f).
- **M4, K3 DockQ:**
  - `eps_eval = up2(max(0.001, 2·Me))`, where Me is the maximum DockQ error over pairs with identical transforms.
  - Defensible iff eps_eval ≤ 0.01 and every fixture has at least 4 CPU-self pairs.
- **M5 and M6, K6/K7:** `0.01 + 2·eps_eval`. Defensible iff M4 is.
- **Run-level conditions:**
  - If the run fails (V0), every derived margin is indefensible.
  - If any fixture comparison has fewer than 4 present pairs on any fixture (Z), every derived margin is indefensible.
  - An indefensible margin keeps its uncertainty: the main run records that output with `exact` (errors recorded) and claims no tolerance.
- **Applying it without judgment:** a later step reads `C/comparison_scored.json` (agrees, missing, max_abs_error, max_rel_error per pair) and A0's fetched `docking.out` (d, N_f), evaluates the formulas, and copies the margins into the main design. After the main run it checks binary, library, driver and GPU identity against the fixture run's `comparison_compute.json` (§3).

Every constant is in the rule's table. k = 2, 0.001 and 0.01 are DESIGN choices, each stated with its reason. Nothing in the rule reads a seed case's output.

## D. The fixture run

- **Design:** `fixture_design.json`, in the exact schema of `SCHEMAS.md:117–141`.
- **Arms:**
  - A0 is the published baseline: CPU standard plus reconstruction.
  - A1 is the GPU standard arm whose outputs K1–K3 compare.
  - A2 and A3 duplicate A0 and A1 with identical commands. This gives two self-agreement arms: CPU, and GPU, which matters because the GPU is the nondeterministic one.
  - The dense arm is not included. No fixture margin concerns it; eps_eval for K6/K7 is an evaluator property measured on A0–A3.
  - The commands are `megadock`/`megadock-gpu` with the run6 flags. Reconstruction is one `bash -c` loop over `decoygen` plus model assembly, because 50 `decoygen` calls exceed the 8-command limit.
- **Inputs:** the four fixtures only.
- **Outputs:** `transforms` and `scores` (regex selections of the 7-field rows of `docking.out`), `coords` (PDB columns 31–54 of `out/model_*.pdb`, natural order) and `dockq` (`eval/dockq.json`, a JSON array).
- **Metric:** the trusted wall, which is required (at least 1 metric) and is not compared.
- **Evaluator:** yes. K3, and through it K6/K7, need it. The native complexes are the evaluator's private data.
- **Comparisons:** 12, all `exact`: four outputs × {cross, CPU self, GPU self}.
  - They decide nothing used by the rule except byte identity, which is itself a recorded fact.
  - The scorer records max_abs_error and max_rel_error for `exact` comparisons too (`score_comparison.py:492–504`), so the rule gets its numbers from the trusted scorer and no agent computes one.
  - Exact checks have no margin, so they cannot bias the rule.
- **Schedule and limits:**
  - `replicates` 6 and `warmup` 1, so 7 rounds × 16 = 112 invocations.
  - `timeout_s` 1200 per arm part and evaluator `timeout_s` 900. Both are far above the expected walls and only cap a hang.
  - `budget_s` 12600, which is below 19800.
  - `order_seed` 27277, `bootstrap_seed` 27278 and `bootstrap_resamples` 1000 (unused, but required by the schema).
- **Projection.**
  - **Per invocation:** about 30 s of overhead (shakedown-m5 run20: job receipt median 8.0 s, comparison receipt median 29.5 s). On top of that come the arm walls:
    - CPU about 5–25 s, scaled by input size from run6's 9.0–14.5 s (`s07:38–41`);
    - GPU about 2–6 s;
    - the evaluator about 2–5 s (run4: 1.8–2.6 s).
  - **Evaluate stage:** about 112 × 30 s plus about 22 min of compute, roughly 78 min.
  - **Rest of the allocation:** intake, harness, the two builds plus the PINDER install, setup, anchors, the users step, fetches and scoring, about 35 min (run6's whole allocation was 2083 s, including about 10 min of jobs; `s07:214`).
  - **Expected:** about 1.9–2.2 h, or **USD 6.3–7.2** at USD 3.29/h.
  - **Worst case under the caps:** about 0.6 h + 3.5 h (`budget_s`) + 0.3 h ≈ 4.4 h, or **USD 14.5**. That is under USD 20 and inside the 6 h limit.
- **Main runs fit after:** USD 100 − 1.67 − 14.5 (worst) = USD 83.8 left. The physical card's whole plan is USD 49.48 (`s13/ASSESSMENT.md:86`), and an agreement run on four cases (about 1.5 h, about USD 5) fits before it. So the answer is yes.
- **Brief:** `FIXTURE_BRIEF.md`.
  - It holds the seed and materials addendum, written from the read text of `BRIEF_run1.md` with the file tool. No byte copy was possible, so the operator should confirm that its first 310 lines equal `BRIEF_run1.md` byte for byte.
  - It then has one section, `## Comparison request (science step s27)`.
  - That section and the view text state no margin, threshold, expected result or rule. I grepped both files for every sealed number of the design (900, 1200, 12600, 27277, 27278, 1000). The only hits outside the sealed fields are digit runs inside SHA-256 hex strings of the verbatim addendum.

## E. What each fixture result decides

- **All of M2–M4 defensible** (with M5 and M6):
  - The next step writes the main agreement design (s13 run 1: A0 and A1, the four seed cases, the same outputs) with K1 transforms `exact`, K1 coordinates `{abs: eps_xyz}`, K2 `{abs: atol, rel: rtol}` and K3 `{abs: eps_eval}`. It writes the main study design with K6/K7 `{abs: 0.01 + 2·eps_eval}`, gated by `given` on K1–K3.
  - The cost then follows s13 and the card.
- **G_T true (GPU transforms not self-reproducible on fixtures):**
  - The card's exact gate (PC:58) would very likely fail on the seed cases from GPU nondeterminism alone.
  - Relaxing it "requires new prospective plan" (PC:66). That is the owner's decision, so the next step stops with `needs_owner` before the main agreement run, rather than spending on a gate that the fixtures show a correct GPU arm cannot pass.
  - The margins M2–M4 still stand or fall by the rule.
- **Some of M2–M4 indefensible:** that comparison is recorded as `exact` with errors and reported as having no defensible tolerance, so agreement is unresolved for it.
  - Whether the acceleration and quality comparisons may still run ungated by it is the owner's decision. The card gates dense quality on agreement failure, and unresolved is not failure. So the next step returns `needs_owner` with the reasons the rule produced.
- **The fixture run fails (V0 or Z):**
  - On an infrastructure failure with no comparison data, one repeat of this exact design is justified within the remaining ceiling.
  - On a harness or evaluator defect, the next step reports it and identifies the contract or harness gap.
  - No margin is derived from a partial run.

## F. Narrowing

Unchanged: **no narrowing** (`NARROWING.md`). The fixtures are measuring instruments, not new cases. The seed's conclusions stay limited to its four cases.

## Predictions and outcomes

s26 sealed no predictions, so `outcomes.json` is `{"items": []}`. Sixteen predictions for the fixture run are sealed in `PREDICTIONS.md` and `predictions.json`.

86	3. **Count mismatch.** If any present pair of F-K4, F-K5 or F-K6 has `agrees` false and `max_rel_error` null, the margin is **indefensible** with reason `score_count_mismatch`.
87	4. **Per-fixture maxima.** For each f:
88	   - MRx_f = the maximum `max_rel_error` over the present F-K4 pairs of f;
89	   - MRc_f = the same over F-K5;
90	   - MRg_f = the same over F-K6.
91	   - A pair that agrees counts 0.
92	   - MR = the maximum of all of them.
93	5. **Margin.** `rtol = up2(max(k·MR, r_floor))`.
94	6. **Defensible iff** step 3 passes and, for every fixture f, max(MRx_f, MRc_f, MRg_f) ≤ A_rel(N_f). Otherwise it is **indefensible** with reason `score_difference_exceeds_analytic_bound`.
95	
96	### M4: main K3, DockQ, `eps_eval` (abs)
97	1. **Qualifying pairs.** Q_e = the present dockq pairs (n ∈ {10,11,12}, f, r) whose pair (t(n), f, r) is present with `agrees` true.
98	2. **Count mismatch.** If any pair in Q_e has `agrees` false and `max_abs_error` null, the margin is **indefensible** with reason `dockq_count_mismatch`.
99	3. **CPU baseline.** If any fixture has fewer than 4 F-K11 pairs in Q_e, the margin is **indefensible** with reason `no_cpu_self_baseline`.
100	4. **Measured value.** Me = the maximum `max_abs_error` over Q_e, with a pair that agrees counting 0.
101	5. **Margin.** `eps_eval = up2(max(e_floor, k·Me))`.
102	6. **Defensible iff** steps 2–3 pass and eps_eval ≤ e_ceiling. Otherwise it is **indefensible** with reason `evaluator_not_repeatable`.
103	
104	### M5 and M6: main K6 (rank-1 DockQ) and main K7 (best-of-50 DockQ), `{abs: m_q + 2·eps_eval}`
105	- The margin is `m_q + 2·eps_eval`.
106	- It is defensible iff M4 is defensible. Otherwise it is **indefensible** with reason `eps_eval_indefensible`.
107	
108	## 3. Applying the margins to a main run (no judgment)
109	
110	1. **Carrying the margins.** The science step that writes the main agreement design copies the following into the main comparisons' `margin` fields, unchanged:
111	   - `eps_xyz` → main K1 coords, `elementwise_abs`;
112	   - `{atol, rtol}` → main K2, `elementwise_abs_plus_rel_max`;
113	   - `eps_eval` → main K3, `elementwise_abs`;
114	   - `m_q + 2·eps_eval` → main K6/K7.
115	2. **Matching definitions.** The main design reuses, byte for byte:
116	   - the four outputs (`name`, `format`, `select`);
117	   - F-A0's and F-A1's commands and `env` for main A0 and A1, with the main inputs' prepared paths in place of the fixtures';
118	   - the evaluator `spec`, apart from the private data's source.
119	3. **Indefensible margins.** For each indefensible margin, the main comparison still records the output with comparator `exact`, so its errors are recorded. The report states "no defensible tolerance (reason …)" and claims neither agreement nor disagreement for that comparison. Whether dependent comparisons proceed without it is the owner's decision (`ASSESSMENT.md` §E).
120	4. **Software and hardware identity.** After the main run, the later step checks the following against the fixture run's `Y.system`. If any check fails, every margin is reported as "not applicable to this main run (software or hardware differs from the fixture run)", and the outcomes are recorded unchanged.
121	   - (a) `executables` for megadock (A0), megadock-gpu (A1) and the evaluator have the same `sha256`, and the same set of library (`name`, `sha256`) rows;
122	   - (b) `driver_version` and `cuda_version` are equal;
123	   - (c) the GPU `name` is equal.
124	5. **Grid size disclosure.** After the main run, if any main input's grid N (the first token of A0's `docking.out`) exceeds max_f N_f, the report states that the score margin was extrapolated in grid size. The margin is still applied.
125	
126	## 4. What this rule does not do
127	- It never reads an output of the main inputs.
128	- It never uses the main arms' differences.
129	- It never widens a margin after a main result.
130	- It does not validate the evaluator's absolute accuracy against an independent DockQ implementation, which the card's "independent DockQ-component checker" (PC:59) asks for. No published arm on this route provides one, so that uncertainty is kept and stated (`ASSESSMENT.md` §B, source 9).

# Tolerance rule for the main comparison's margins (science step s27, sealed before any fixture result)

This rule turns the fixture run's recorded values (`fixture_design.json` in this folder, run by m5 in comparison mode) and the analytic budget (`ASSESSMENT.md` §B) into the margins of the main comparison. It is fixed now. No constant, condition or step below may change after any fixture or main result exists. A later step applies it mechanically: every quantity is read from named files, and every decision is a comparison of numbers.

## 0. Names

**Main comparison.** These are s13's `FINAL.json` K1–K3 and K6/K7 (A1 against A0, and A2 against A1) on the four seed cases.
- Main K1 has two parts: transform identity (the card's exact criterion) and reconstructed coordinates within `eps_xyz`.
- Main K2 compares scores within `atol + rtol·max(|a|,|b|)`.
- Main K3 compares per-model DockQ within `eps_eval`.
- Main K6/K7 use the margin `0.01 + 2·eps_eval` (PC:29).

**Fixture run arms.** In `fixture_design.json`:
- F-A0 is main A0 (CPU standard);
- F-A1 is main A1 (GPU standard);
- F-A2 runs F-A0's commands again;
- F-A3 runs F-A1's commands again.

**Fixture comparisons.** These are the design's ids K1–K12, written F-K1 … F-K12 here so they are not confused with the main K ids. Every one is `exact`. The scorer records for each (fixture, replicate) pair: `agrees` (byte identity of the selected content), `missing`, `max_abs_error` and `max_rel_error`. The errors are computed over the parsed numbers, with rel = |a−b| / max(|a|,|b|) (`dut/pipeline/m5/score_comparison.py:469–504`).

| output | cross: F-A1 vs F-A0 | CPU self: F-A2 vs F-A0 | GPU self: F-A3 vs F-A1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| transforms | F-K1 | F-K2 | F-K3 |
| scores | F-K4 | F-K5 | F-K6 |
| coords | F-K7 | F-K8 | F-K9 |
| dockq | F-K10 | F-K11 | F-K12 |

For each output row, `t(n)` is the transforms comparison of the same arm pair:
- t(7) = t(10) = 1;
- t(8) = t(11) = 2;
- t(9) = t(12) = 3.

**Files.** All are in the fixture run's folder:
- `S` = `control/C/comparison_scored.json`, or the run's `C/comparison_scored.json` wherever the run keeps `C/`;
- `O(arm, f, r)` = the fetched `A/results/evaluate/comparison/r<r>/<arm>/<f>/out/docking.out`;
- `Y` = `A/results/evaluate/comparison_compute.json`.

**Pairs.** `pairs(n, f)` is the `pairs` list of the row with `input == f` of comparison F-Kn in `S`. A pair is *present* when `missing` is false. The fixtures are f1a19, f1dtd, f1glj and f1ht8.

**Constants (all fixed now).**

| symbol | value | basis |
|---|---|---|
| u | 2^-24 | IEEE-754 binary32 unit roundoff. Both arms' FFTs are single precision: `-lfftw3f` on the CPU and cuFFT with `-use_fast_math` on the GPU (`science/s06/CALIBRATION_BRIEF.md:361–369`). |
| k | 2 | DESIGN. Headroom from the maximum over the fixture sample (4 fixtures × 6 replicates × 50 values per output) to new inputs. |
| r_floor | 1e-6 | ≈ 17u. This covers two independent binary32 roundings plus a few operations. Below it, a relative tolerance is not resolvable in single precision. |
| xyz_unit | 0.001 Å | One unit in the last place of PDB coordinates (%8.3f). |
| e_floor | 0.001 | DESIGN. The smallest DockQ difference the study reports (three decimals). |
| e_ceiling | 0.01 | DESIGN. This equals the card's K6/K7 quality margin (PC:29, 270–274). An evaluator that disagrees with itself on identical models by more than the study's quality margin cannot support K6/K7. |
| A_rel(N) | (3·log2(N³) + 1) · 5u · N^1.5 | A worst-case relative error of one correlation peak from three single-precision FFTs on an N³ grid (`ASSESSMENT.md` §B, source 1). |
| m_q | 0.01 | The card's DESIGN quality margin for K6/K7 (PC:29), used unchanged. |

**Rounding.** `up2(x)` is the smallest number of the form m·10^e (m an integer from 10 to 99, e an integer) that is ≥ x. Every margin is reported as `up2` of its formula, except `atol` and `xyz_unit`, which are exact powers of ten.

## 1. Validity and completeness (applied first)

- **V0.** `S` exists, and its `comparison_sha256` equals the run's `C/comparison_seal.json`. The run's evaluate stage is PASS.
  - If V0 fails, every margin M2–M6 is **indefensible** with reason `fixture_run_failed`. M1 keeps its exact criterion, and its flags are `unknown`.
- **Z.** For every n in 1..12 and every fixture f, `pairs(n, f)` holds at least 4 present pairs.
  - If Z fails, M2–M6 are **indefensible** with reason `fixture_incomplete`. M1's flags are computed on the present pairs and marked `incomplete`.

## 2. The margins

### M1: main K1, transform identity (exact; no tolerance)
- **Margin.** `null`, with comparator `exact`. The card seals exact ranked rotation/translation identity, including rank 1 and cutoff membership, and "Tie mismatch fails this strict gate" (PC:58). The card also says "any relaxed policy requires new prospective plan" (PC:66). The fixture run derives no tolerance here.
- **Flags** (always reported):
  - `X_T` = some present F-K1 pair has `agrees` false;
  - `C_T` = the same for F-K2;
  - `G_T` = the same for F-K3.
- **Use in the main report.** If `G_T` is true, the main report must state that GPU-standard transforms were not reproducible against themselves on disjoint fixtures. A main K1 "not supported" then cannot be attributed to CPU/GPU disagreement alone.
- M1 is a sealed criterion, not a derived tolerance, so it has no defensibility test.

### M2: main K1, coordinates, `eps_xyz` (abs, Å)
1. **Qualifying pairs.** Q = the present coords pairs (n ∈ {7,8,9}, f, r) whose pair (t(n), f, r) is present with `agrees` true.
2. **Count mismatch.** If any pair in Q has `agrees` false and `max_abs_error` null, the margin is **indefensible** with reason `coords_count_mismatch`.
3. **CPU baseline.** If any fixture has fewer than 4 F-K8 pairs in Q, the margin is **indefensible** with reason `no_cpu_self_baseline`.
4. **Measured value.** Mxyz = the maximum `max_abs_error` over Q, with a pair that agrees counting 0.
5. **Margin.** `eps_xyz = up2(max(xyz_unit, k·Mxyz))`.
6. **Defensible iff** steps 2–3 pass and Mxyz ≤ xyz_unit. Otherwise it is **indefensible** with reason `reconstruction_not_deterministic`.

### M3: main K2, scores, `{abs: atol, rel: rtol}`
1. **Print resolution.**
   - d = the maximum number of digits after the decimal point among the last-field tokens of the 7-field rows of every present `O(A0, f, r)`. d is 0 if no token has a point.
   - `atol = 10^-d`.
2. **Grid size.** N_f = `int(float(t))`, where t is the first whitespace-separated token of the first line of `O(A0, f, r_min)`, and r_min is the lowest replicate whose file exists.
3. **Count mismatch.** If any present pair of F-K4, F-K5 or F-K6 has `agrees` false and `max_rel_error` null, the margin is **indefensible** with reason `score_count_mismatch`.
4. **Per-fixture maxima.** For each f:
   - MRx_f = the maximum `max_rel_error` over the present F-K4 pairs of f;
   - MRc_f = the same over F-K5;
   - MRg_f = the same over F-K6.
   - A pair that agrees counts 0.
   - MR = the maximum of all of them.
5. **Margin.** `rtol = up2(max(k·MR, r_floor))`.
6. **Defensible iff** step 3 passes and, for every fixture f, max(MRx_f, MRc_f, MRg_f) ≤ A_rel(N_f). Otherwise it is **indefensible** with reason `score_difference_exceeds_analytic_bound`.

### M4: main K3, DockQ, `eps_eval` (abs)
1. **Qualifying pairs.** Q_e = the present dockq pairs (n ∈ {10,11,12}, f, r) whose pair (t(n), f, r) is present with `agrees` true.
2. **Count mismatch.** If any pair in Q_e has `agrees` false and `max_abs_error` null, the margin is **indefensible** with reason `dockq_count_mismatch`.
3. **CPU baseline.** If any fixture has fewer than 4 F-K11 pairs in Q_e, the margin is **indefensible** with reason `no_cpu_self_baseline`.
4. **Measured value.** Me = the maximum `max_abs_error` over Q_e, with a pair that agrees counting 0.
5. **Margin.** `eps_eval = up2(max(e_floor, k·Me))`.
6. **Defensible iff** steps 2–3 pass and eps_eval ≤ e_ceiling. Otherwise it is **indefensible** with reason `evaluator_not_repeatable`.

### M5 and M6: main K6 (rank-1 DockQ) and main K7 (best-of-50 DockQ), `{abs: m_q + 2·eps_eval}`
- The margin is `m_q + 2·eps_eval`.
- It is defensible iff M4 is defensible. Otherwise it is **indefensible** with reason `eps_eval_indefensible`.

## 3. Applying the margins to a main run (no judgment)

1. **Carrying the margins.** The science step that writes the main agreement design copies the following into the main comparisons' `margin` fields, unchanged:
   - `eps_xyz` → main K1 coords, `elementwise_abs`;
   - `{atol, rtol}` → main K2, `elementwise_abs_plus_rel_max`;
   - `eps_eval` → main K3, `elementwise_abs`;
   - `m_q + 2·eps_eval` → main K6/K7.
2. **Matching definitions.** The main design reuses, byte for byte:
   - the four outputs (`name`, `format`, `select`);
   - F-A0's and F-A1's commands and `env` for main A0 and A1, with the main inputs' prepared paths in place of the fixtures';
   - the evaluator `spec`, apart from the private data's source.
3. **Indefensible margins.** For each indefensible margin, the main comparison still records the output with comparator `exact`, so its errors are recorded. The report states "no defensible tolerance (reason …)" and claims neither agreement nor disagreement for that comparison. Whether dependent comparisons proceed without it is the owner's decision (`ASSESSMENT.md` §E).
4. **Software and hardware identity.** After the main run, the later step checks the following against the fixture run's `Y.system`. If any check fails, every margin is reported as "not applicable to this main run (software or hardware differs from the fixture run)", and the outcomes are recorded unchanged.
   - (a) `executables` for megadock (A0), megadock-gpu (A1) and the evaluator have the same `sha256`, and the same set of library (`name`, `sha256`) rows;
   - (b) `driver_version` and `cuda_version` are equal;
   - (c) the GPU `name` is equal.
5. **Grid size disclosure.** After the main run, if any main input's grid N (the first token of A0's `docking.out`) exceeds max_f N_f, the report states that the score margin was extrapolated in grid size. The margin is still applied.

## 4. What this rule does not do
- It never reads an output of the main inputs.
- It never uses the main arms' differences.
- It never widens a margin after a main result.
- It does not validate the evaluator's absolute accuracy against an independent DockQ implementation, which the card's "independent DockQ-component checker" (PC:59) asks for. No published arm on this route provides one, so that uncertainty is kept and stated (`ASSESSMENT.md` §B, source 9).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
: "${CMP_INPUT:?}" "${CMP_INPUT_SPEC:?}" "${CMP_PRIVATE:?}" "${CMP_ARM_OUT:?}" "${CMP_EVAL_OUT:?}"
mkdir -p "$CMP_EVAL_OUT"
# The interpreter and installed evaluator live beside the shared published source.
VPY="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")")/../baseline-published/evaluator-venv/bin/python"
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
export XDG_CACHE_HOME="$CMP_EVAL_OUT/cache" MPLCONFIGDIR="$CMP_EVAL_OUT/matplotlib"
export TMPDIR="$CMP_EVAL_OUT/tmp"
mkdir -p "$TMPDIR"
"$VPY" - <<'PY' >> "$CMP_EVAL_OUT/evaluator.log" 2>&1
import os,json,pathlib,hashlib,math
from pinder.eval.dockq import BiotiteDockQ
from pinder.core.structure.atoms import atom_array_from_pdb_file
spec=json.loads(os.environ['CMP_INPUT_SPEC'])
private=pathlib.Path(os.environ['CMP_PRIVATE']).resolve()
ref=spec['reference'];native=(private/ref['name']).resolve()
if not native.is_relative_to(private):raise RuntimeError('Reference outside CMP_PRIVATE')
b=native.read_bytes()
if len(b)!=ref['bytes'] or hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()!=ref['sha256']:raise RuntimeError('Native checksum mismatch')
arm=pathlib.Path(os.environ['CMP_ARM_OUT']).resolve()
out=pathlib.Path(os.environ['CMP_EVAL_OUT']).resolve()
chains=list(dict.fromkeys(atom_array_from_pdb_file(native).chain_id.tolist()))
if 'R' in chains and 'L' in chains: receptor,ligand='R','L'
elif len(chains)==2: receptor,ligand=chains
else: raise RuntimeError('Native receptor/ligand chain mapping is ambiguous')
models=[arm/f'model_{r}.pdb' for r in range(1,51)]
for p in models:
    if not p.is_file():raise RuntimeError('Missing model: '+str(p))
result=BiotiteDockQ(native=native,decoys=models,
    native_receptor_chain=[receptor],native_ligand_chain=[ligand],
    decoy_receptor_chain=['R'],decoy_ligand_chain=['L']).calculate()
# Upstream can reorder unequal atom-count models; restore the sealed rank order.
result=result.set_index('model_name').loc[[p.stem for p in models]].reset_index()
values=[float(x) for x in result['DockQ']]
if len(values)!=50 or not all(math.isfinite(x) for x in values):raise RuntimeError('Invalid DockQ output')
result.to_csv(out/'components.csv',index=False)
(out/'dockq.json').write_text(json.dumps(values,allow_nan=False)+'\n')
PY

115:## Sealed comparison (U57, U58)

115 ## Sealed comparison (U57, U58) 116 - Purpose: compare several published arms on one box under a design fixed before the run. Owner approval 2026-11-03 (contract gaps G1 comparison arms, G3 tolerance and equivalence, G6 compute metadata of the blind-02 science route); requirements from science steps s13 to s23. Arms are published programs or configurations that need no new code, run by the pipeline from sealed argument vectors. Each invocation runs one arm on one input, and invocations are interleaved on one box. No agent computes a number: every number comes from the pipeline's trusted wall time, from rules fixed before the run and applied by the pipeline, from a trusted comparator of two arms' outputs, or from a published evaluator that runs on each arm's output without access to the arm's identity. Criteria, margins, thresholds, reference values and timeouts are fixed by a science step before the run, sealed, and unreadable by the run's agents and by the processes of arms and evaluator. Compute is recorded twice and never mixed: per invocation as attribution and per box allocation as the bill. Never change a criterion after a result: every decision uses the sealed design. An outcome that is not supported is a result and never fails a stage. Comparisons that need more than one run are split by the science step into one design per run; a design whose launch depends on an earlier run's outcomes is launched only when the science step finds them in that run's `C/comparison_scored.json`. Without `args.comparison`, every stage is unchanged. Declared residual risks, which no rule below removes: the evaluator reads the arm's output files by design, so file names or content under `out/` that identify the program can reach it (the sealed `evaluate.sh` bytes make any dependence on them auditable after the run); state of shared hardware (device memory, caches, timing) is not cleared between parts; a harness script that disobeys the rule that only `fetch_private.sh` handles the evaluator's private data can leave a transformed copy of them (an archive, a re-encoding, a derived file) where the arm part can read it, which the byte-identity check of Separated users step 7 does not detect (`setup.sh` and its repairs are kept in `A/harness/` and the stage's receipts, so such a copy is auditable after the run); and processes, shell start-up hooks or scheduled jobs that `setup.sh`, its repairs or the anchors leave behind run as the box user, which the pipeline's own box commands also use, so they can read and change what the box user can (the same kept bytes make them auditable; the hash check of Separated users step 1 detects a sealed harness file changed before it). 117 - Optional `args.comparison` is an object with exactly the key `design`: a non-empty path, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory, to a design JSON file. It is exclusive with `args.card`, `args.units_check` and `args.units_probe`. The design is exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, evaluator, replicates, warmup, order_seed, timeout_s, budget_s, bootstrap_seed, bootstrap_resamples, comparisons}`: 118 - `arms`: 2 to 5 items, each exactly `{id, what, commands, env}`; ids `"A0"`, `"A1"`, ... in order; `what` a non-empty string. `A0` is the published baseline that intake and reproduce handle as usual. 119 - `commands`: 1 to 8 commands, each a non-empty array of non-empty strings: the exact published command lines of the arm, in order, as argument vectors run without a shell. The pipeline runs them (see Evaluate); the arm's adapter only prepares. 120 - `env`: null or an object mapping names that match `^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$` and do not start with `CMP_` to strings; set for the arm's commands. 121 - Placeholders, in command and `env` strings only: `{input}` (the input id), `{run}`, `{out}` (the absolute paths of the invocation's `run/` and `out/`) and `{spec:

}` with `

Rows of `not_run` invocations have null numbers. 185 - `arms` has one row per arm, each exactly `{arm, invocations, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known, eval_wall_s, eval_gpu_busy_s, attributed_usd}`, summed over that arm's replicate invocations whatever their status, with a null counted as 0; `gpu_busy_known` is true only when every summed row's flag is. 186 - `all_invocations` is exactly `{invocations, wall_s, eval_wall_s, attributed_usd}`, summed over every row, warmups and failures included, with a null counted as 0. 187 - `system` and `versions` copy the fetched `system.json` and `versions.json` (null when missing or invalid). 188 - `allocation` is the bill of the whole box allocation, which may include work outside this run, exactly `{type, price_usd_h, started_utc, ended_utc, hours, usd, final}` from `C/box.json`. When that record has `ended_utc` and `hours`, they are copied and `final` is true; otherwise `ended_utc` is null, `hours` is the time from `started_utc` to when the file is written, and `final` is false. `usd` is `hours * price_usd_h`. Unavailable fields are null. At takeaways, after a matching allocation record refreshes `C/box.json` (see Compute metadata), the pipeline rewrites the file atomically with only `allocation` recomputed. The run's own share stays `run_box_usd`. 189 Uploads, links, job files, user setup, the private-data fetch and removal, cleanups and fetches are outside every invocation row; they remain in the stage's receipts. 190 - Scoring (U58): after the last invocation, `python3 -I m5/score_comparison.py `. It checks the SHA-256 of `C/comparison.json` against `C/comparison_seal.json` and of each sealed harness file against `C/arms_seal.json`, then scores each comparison, in design order, from the replicate rounds only. 191 - Locations: a relative path names one file. A `{glob}` location names the regular files that Python `glob.glob(glob, root_dir=)` returns, sorted by a key that splits the relative path into runs of digits and non-digits, compares digit runs as integers and breaks ties by the path; their contents, each after `select`, are joined by `"\n"` (by `b"\n"` for `bytes`). A side of an (input, replicate) pair is missing when its invocation's status is not `ok`, when the location is under `eval` and `eval_status` is not `ok`, when the location names no file or an unreadable one, when the content cannot be parsed as the output's `format`, or when the selected content is empty (no bytes for `bytes`, no numbers otherwise). 192 - Output comparisons (`agreement`): for each input and replicate where neither side is missing, the comparator compares the two contents. `exact`: identical bytes. Otherwise both contents are parsed as the output's `format` into number lists; different lengths, or a NaN in one list but not at the same position in the other, disagree; equal infinities agree; finite pairs agree when `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol` (`elementwise_abs`) or `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol + rel_tol * max(abs(a), abs(b))` (`elementwise_abs_plus_rel_max`). A pair agrees when every element agrees. Each compared pair records `max_abs_error` and `max_rel_error` over its finite elements (null when none). 193 - Metric comparisons: an arm's value for (replicate, input) is the metric value above. For `pooled_mean`, a replicate's value is the mean over inputs, null when any input's value is null. Per decision unit (the pooled value, or each input): for `paired_replicate`, the differences are `arm - against` per replicate; for `unpaired`, the differences of every arm value with every against value, or of every arm value with the input's reference value. `ratio_at_least` uses the ratio of means `mean(arm) / mean(against)` for `higher_better` and `mean(against) / mean(arm)` for `lower_better`. 194 - Missing values, per decision unit: `n_missing` counts the arm's missing values and, against an arm, the against arm's (for `pooled_mean` a replicate counts once; for agreement a pair with a missing side counts once). With `"void"`, any missing value makes the unit void with reason `"missing_values"`. With `"fail"`, a missing value of `arm` makes the unit `"not_supported"` with reason `"missing_values"`, and otherwise a missing value of `against` makes it void with reason `"missing_values"`. 195 - Eligibility (`given`): for each listed comparison, its outcome for this unit is that comparison's row for the same input when both comparisons are decided per input, and otherwise that comparison's outcome, where `"per_input"` counts as supported only when every row is. When any of these is not `"supported"`, the unit is void with reason `"not_eligible"`. 196 - Interval: for `all_pairs`, `[lo, hi]` is the minimum and maximum of the differences, and needs at least one difference. For `bootstrap`, the ratio of means is recomputed on `bootstrap_resamples` resamples (`B`) with replacement of the unit's paired replicates, drawn from one `random.Random(bootstrap_seed)` stream in comparison order, and `[lo, hi]` is the `(1 - confidence) / 2` and `(1 + confidence) / 2` empirical quantiles (sorted resamples, index `floor(q * (B - 1))`); it needs at least two replicates. `estimate` is the mean difference (`all_pairs`) or the ratio of means (`bootstrap`) on the full data. Too few values gives outcome `"void"` with reason `"insufficient_replicates"`. 197 - Margin value `m`: 0 for a null margin, `x` for `{"abs": x}`. 198 - Outcome per decision unit, in this order: eligibility; then, for agreement, any compared pair that disagrees makes the unit not supported; then the missing-value rule; then the interval's minimum count; then the criterion. The criterion gives `"supported"`, `"not_supported"` or else `"inconclusive"`: agreement is supported when at least one pair was compared, every compared pair agrees and none is missing (with no compared pair, it is void with reason `"missing_values"`); non-inferiority (`higher_better`) is supported when `lo >= -m`, not supported when `hi < -m`; non-inferiority (`lower_better`) is supported when `hi <= m`, not supported when `lo > m`; superiority (`two_sided`) is supported when `lo > m` or `hi < -m`, not supported when `-m <= lo` and `hi <= m`; ratio with `strict` false is supported when `lo >= threshold`, not supported when `hi < threshold`; ratio with `strict` true is supported when `lo > threshold`, not supported when `hi <= threshold`. 199 - `sign` of a unit is `"higher"` when a superiority is supported with `lo > m`, `"lower"` when it is supported with `hi < -m`, and null otherwise. 200 - A comparison's outcome: for `pooled_mean`, its one unit's outcome; for `per_input_all`, supported when every input is supported, not supported when any input is not supported, void when any input is void and none is not supported, otherwise inconclusive; for `per_input_each`, `"per_input"`, with each input's outcome in its rows. 201 - `C/comparison_scored.json`, atomic, is exactly `{comparison_sha256, comparisons, totals}`. `comparisons` follows the design's order, each exactly `{id, arm, against, criterion, unit, outcome, rows}`; `rows` has one row per decision unit (`input` null for `pooled_mean`), each exactly `{input, n, n_missing, estimate, lo, hi, margin_value, threshold, outcome, sign, reason, pairs}`. `n` counts the differences, ratios or compared pairs; `pairs` is null for metric comparisons and, for agreement, the per-replicate rows `{replicate, agrees, missing, max_abs_error, max_rel_error}` (`agrees` null and `missing` true when a side is missing). Numbers are null when void; `reason` is `"missing_values"`, `"insufficient_replicates"` or `"not_eligible"` for a void unit, `"missing_values"` for a unit made not supported by the `"fail"` rule, and null otherwise. `totals` is exactly `{supported, not_supported, inconclusive, void}`, counting decision units over all comparisons. 202 - Exit 0 after writing; exit 1 for invalid or missing input (a design that intake would reject included), a seal mismatch or a failed write, with no output file. A missing or invalid `wrap.json` or fetched file is not invalid input; it is a missing value. Diagnostics contain no input content. A scoring failure fails evaluate with `error_class: parse`. 203 - Evaluate status in comparison mode is PASS once `C/comparison_scored.json` was written, whatever the outcomes. Evaluate facts keep every existing key, null in comparison mode. 204 205 ## A/results/profile/ and A/profile-packet.json 206 - Profile fetches remote `out/` to `A/results/profile/out/`; logs are `A/results/profile/.log`. Its inputs are therefore under `A/results/profile/out/profile/`. Remote `out/profile/` is cleared before profiling to prevent stale evidence from passing. 207 - The pipeline uploads trusted `m5/profile_nsys.sh`, `m5/profile_summarise.py` and the collected probe into remote `profiler/`. Through boxrun, it invokes `bash profiler/profile_nsys.sh harness/run_command.sh out/profile `. The profiler reuses `nsys` from PATH or NVIDIA installation paths. Otherwise it tries `nsight-systems-cli` with apt using only source files listed by the probe, without enabling commented repositories or adding sources. If unavailable, it downloads the official Ubuntu 22.04 amd64 CLI package `NsightSystems-linux-cli-public-2025.3.1.90-3582212.deb` from `https://developer.download.nvidia.com/devtools/repos/ubuntu2204/amd64/` into a temporary directory outside `out/` that is removed after installation (the package never reaches `out/` or fetched results), verifies the SHA-256 pinned in the script, installs with `sudo -n dpkg -i` and runs `sudo -n apt-get -f install -y` for dependencies using the image's existing sources without adding repositories. This fixed profiler installation is an exception to the setup-script installation restrictions above. The profiler prepends the discovered Nsight binary directory to PATH. Missing tools, installation failures and collection/export failures emit `M5_PROFILER_INFRA`, write `out/profile/infra.json`, and exit 2; the pipeline classifies these as `infra` without agent calls. 208 - Collection uses `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=none` around the shared command without modifying its environment. An inner launcher measures only that command with a monotonic clock; installation, profiler finalization and CSV export are excluded. The command's output is preserved in `baseline.log` as well as its own saved logs. Export uses `nsys stats --report cuda_gpu_kern_sum,cuda_gpu_mem_time_sum,cuda_api_sum --format csv`. Raw report, CSV files, tool version, export log, `raw_wall_s.json` and `gpu_util_raw.jsonl` remain in `out/profile/`. 209 - `python3 m5/profile_summarise.py ` deterministically writes the three existing profile files. CSV total time/duration units ns, us/µs, ms and s are converted to seconds. Known Nsight skips for absent kernel/memory/API activity count as zero; missing or malformed reports fail parsing. A report is a known skip when its CSV file carries Nsight's `SKIPPED` line and no header row, or when its CSV file is absent, empty or whitespace-only and `stats.log` in the same directory states that the report does not contain its own activity: `does not contain CUDA kernel data` for `stats_cuda_gpu_kern_sum.csv`, `does not contain GPU memory data` for `stats_cuda_gpu_mem_time_sum.csv`, and `does not contain CUDA trace data` for `stats_cuda_api_sum.csv` (U48). These are Nsight's own wordings; the earlier phrases `CUDA memory data` and `CUDA API data` never occur in Nsight output and no longer count as statements. Nsight Systems 2025 writes an empty file for a skipped report where earlier versions wrote none. An absent, empty or whitespace-only file without that statement for its own activity, and any other missing or malformed report, still fails parsing. Run evidence (blind-01 run9, 2026-11-01): the baseline ran to completion under the profiler with no CUDA activity and no capture problem; Nsight 2025 logged the three skips and wrote three empty summary files, and the summariser failed on a missing CSV header, so profile stopped with `parse` instead of reaching its numeric gate. Replay of the merged U48 summariser on run9's saved files (2026-11-01) still failed: Nsight states the memory and API skips as `GPU memory data` and `CUDA trace data`; with those wordings the summariser exits 0 and the gate reports `numeric` (other host time within 2% of total wall). Five rows are emitted: `kernels` (compute), `memcpy H2D` (transfer), `memcpy D2H` (transfer), `CUDA API host time` (other), and `other host time` (other). GPU seconds retain the raw kernel/transfer sums; host GPU seconds are null. Aggregate CSV reports do not identify critical-path intervals: if the four reported sums exceed measured wall, their wall allocations are scaled proportionally to fit. Other host time is the nonnegative wall remainder. These allocations are an aggregate approximation, not measured exclusive phase durations. No stage timestamps are invented; aggregate rows omit `start_s`, so stage utilisation remains null. No bound uses stage utilisation; same-GPU headroom comes from the concurrency probe. 210 - `stages.json` is an array of `{stage, wall_s, gpu_s}`, optionally including `kind`: `compute`, `transfer`, or `other`, and `start_s`: finite nonnegative elapsed seconds sharing the telemetry clock. Fixed profiler supplies `kind`; legacy rows without it remain accepted. `stage` is a non-empty string; `wall_s` is finite nonnegative seconds; `gpu_s` is finite nonnegative seconds or null and must be present. Fixed profiler wall allocations sum to measured wall without exceeding it; overlapping aggregate durations use the approximation above. Extra input fields are not copied to the packet. Empty arrays parse but fail the numeric gate. 211 - `total_wall_s.json` is an object with finite positive numeric `total_wall_s` in seconds. The sum of stage wall times must also be finite. 212 - `gpu_util.json` is an array of `{t, util}` samples collected with `nvidia-smi` during the measured run. `t` is finite nonnegative elapsed seconds; `util` is a finite GPU utilisation percentage in [0,100]. The fixed sampler records the mean across GPUs returned by nvidia-smi, then the summarizer retains only samples during the shared command and rebases monotonic timestamps to its start. A sample with zero utilisation is valid. Empty arrays parse but fail the numeric gate; missing files or malformed samples fail parsing. 213 - The deterministic pipeline writes `A/profile-packet.json` with exact keys: 214 - `stages`: the validated timing rows, preserving optional `kind`, each augmented with `wall_fraction = min(1, wall_s / total_wall_s)`, `start_s`, and `mean_gpu_util` (fraction in [0,1], or null). When supplied, `start_s` must be measured on the telemetry clock. Legacy rows without `start_s` record null start and utilisation; stage order does not establish a measured telemetry window. Stage endpoints must remain finite. Stage utilisation is the arithmetic mean of telemetry percentages divided by 100 in `[start_s, start_s + wall_s)`; no samples means null. Never substitute GPU busy seconds for utilisation;
